description: Phase 2 parity: in the link browser, Left while drilled goes back (panel stays); Left with a non-empty filter at the top level only edits the filter (panel stays); Left at the top level with an empty filter closes the panel (state, window_id and Quartz agree) and opens nothing
requirement: P2-browser-left-close (GPUI Phase 2 parity, Tauri dist/panel.js:567-569 ArrowLeft + browseBack 367-371)
notes: Tauri reference: ArrowLeft does nothing special while browse.filter is non-empty (the key edits the filter: `if (browse.filter) return;`), whatever the caret position; otherwise browseBack(): at the root it dismisses the panel, when drilled it goes back one level.
graph-backlinks.json seeded; top-level rows in list_links order: Decoy Unrelated, Gamma Doc, Beta Post, ... Gamma Doc's only connection is the subject (browser-drill.json).
Drilled round: one quick check that Left still returns to 'Your links' on route browser with the panel visible (browser-drill.json covers the selection restore).

Filter round: types 'be', then presses Left three times. The first two move the caret to the start of the text inside the Input; the third reaches the browser's bubble-phase MoveLeft at the text's start edge (A11Y-NOTES.md key table). The browser must still not close, because the filter is non-empty (the Tauri rule is about the filter's content, not the caret). Typing 'x' afterwards proves the caret went to the start and the filter is still being edited ('xbe').

Close round: a restart gives a fresh browser with an empty filter (End/Escape are intercepted by the browser, so clearing in place is not a plain keystroke). winframe 'any' records the window number right after the panel opens, so 'gone' checks the hide at the window server.
